title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: TikTok trend
drivers.evidence: No past data for TikTok-driven sales; product has no prior viral event. One-time trend with no historical analog. Noise-adjusted uplift from promotions is x1.45, but this is a new driver. Apply conservative uplift.

drivers.name: Price increase (6%)
drivers.evidence: No past sales at this price. Price increase typically reduces demand. Base trend shows volatility, but no evidence of price insensitivity. Adjust downward for price sensitivity.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 10.2. No events are scheduled, but the price is raised 6% above regular. The product has no history of sales spikes at this price. Past promotions show a median lift of x2.15, but noise-adjusted lift is only x1.45. The TikTok trend is a new driver with no historical parallel. The 2025 Thanksgiving week before event shows a drop (x0.66), but noise-adjusted x1.0, so no downward effect. A 6% price increase typically suppresses demand, but the TikTok trend may override this. The effect is uncertain and speculative. Use median multiplier shrunk toward 1.0.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.08 (+6.0% vs regular price 3.85)
  planner notes: Product is trending on TikTok

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 10.2 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 25.3 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 19.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
